channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro viaja aos EUA para encontro com Trump e avisa Senado
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), a pre-candidate for president, notified the Senate he will be out of the country until Thursday, March 28, after departing for the United States on Sunday, March 24. He intends to meet with U.S. President Donald Trump during the trip.

item.title: Crusoé: Eduardo e Carlos Bolsonaro reagem a Zema
item.description: The Bolsonaro brothers, Carlos and Eduardo, harshly criticized Romeu Zema (Novo), a pre-candidate for president, for claiming that voting for Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) would hand the election to Lula (PT). Carlos, a Senate pre-candidate from Santa Catarina, called Zema 'low' and threatened to 'stab him again' at the first opportunity. Eduardo also reacted, reinforcing the Bolsonaros’ hostility toward the former governor of Minas Gerais.

item.title: O arsenal de IA nas eleições para promover candidatos — e atacar adversários
item.description: Brazil's 2026 elections are expected to feature an arsenal of AI tools to promote candidates and attack opponents, including the use of 'neurobots' (fake digital personas), mass WhatsApp messaging, purchase of followers and comments, automated AI-generated content, data scraping, and automated monitoring of electoral violations. Many of these practices operate in a legal gray zone or are outright illegal, according to BBC News Brasil interviewees who accessed demonstrations of platforms being marketed for campaign use.

item.title: Pesquisas eleitorais: um bom e um mau sinal para Lula na nova BTG Nexus
item.description: Lula leads with 40% voting intention, followed by Flávio Bolsonaro with 35%, according to the BTG Nexus poll. Although Flávio Bolsonaro has surpassed Lula in rejection (50% vs 47%), Lula’s still-high rejection rate poses a risk to winning in the first round.

item.title: PL anuncia novo marqueteiro de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The PL announced the new pre-campaign team for Flávio Bolsonaro, with publicist Eduardo Fischer as strategic communication consultant and Alexandre Oltramari as campaign marketer. Fischer will define the communication guidelines and positioning, while Oltramari will coordinate communication and marketing efforts. The move reflects the party’s effort to structure Flávio Bolsonaro’s candidacy for the 2026 elections.

item.title: ‘Gambá cheira gambá’, diz Zema sobre encontro de Flávio Bolsonaro e Daniel Vorcaro
item.description: Romeu Zema, former governor of Minas Gerais and Novo party presidential pre-candidate, criticized the meeting between Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) and banker Daniel Vorcaro, calling Vorcaro 'the biggest criminal in Brazil' and stating 'like attracts like'. He said the scandal harms the right and that Lula is leading in polls, but affirmed he will support any right-wing candidate against the PT in a potential 2026 runoff, including Bolsonaro, despite his criticism.

item.title: Zema diz que quem votar em Flávio Bolsonaro entregará eleição a Lula; Caiado pede união contra o PT
item.description: Romeu Zema, pre-candidate of the Novo Party, said voting for Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) would likely hand the election to Lula, citing the Banco Master scandal as worsening the right’s prospects. He criticized Bolsonaro’s association with banker Daniel Vorcaro, denied ever meeting him, and advocated for competent candidates over familial ties. Despite his criticism, Zema stated he would maintain some level of support for Bolsonaro, without specifying the nature of that support.

item.title: Zema defende modelo de El Salvador com 'encarceramento em massa' contra o crime
item.description: Romeu Zema, pré-candidate for Presidency from the Novo party, advocated adopting a public security model inspired by El Salvador, featuring mass incarceration, labeling criminals as terrorists, and minimum 25-year sentences without benefits. He cited El Salvador's 99% reduction in homicides over four years as a global success story and said he visited the country with Minas Gerais' public security secretary, claiming unanimous public approval of the measures. Zema called for a 'shock in public security' in Brazil and criticized politicians with ties to denounced figures and the electoral use of family connections.

item.title: Caiado defende uso das Forças Armadas contra facções na Amazônia
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado, pre-candidate for presidency from PSD, advocated for the use of the Armed Forces to combat criminal factions in the Amazon, claiming over half the territory is under their control. He proposed classifying PCC and CV as terrorist organizations and criticized the alleged contamination of the formal economy and institutions, including the STF, by illicit practices.

item.title: Após reunião com Lula, Motta anuncia transição para redução de jornada de trabalho
item.description: Following a meeting with President Lula, Chamber President Hugo Motta announced that the final report on the PEC to end the 6×1 work schedule proposes reducing the weekly workweek from 44 to 40 hours without salary cuts, including a one-year transition period. The implementation will be phased: a two-hour reduction after 60 days of promulgation and another two-hour reduction after 12 months. Reporter Deputy Leo Prates (Republicanos-BA) is expected to present the opinion today, with voting anticipated in the special committee and plenary this week.

item.title: Lula critica ultradireita e alerta para ‘colonialismo digital’ em fórum com reitores africanos
item.description: President Lula criticized the far-right for attacking universities and promoting indoctrination, and warned about 'digital colonialism', stating that algorithms in the hands of a few companies and countries have become instruments of domination. He defended universities as spaces of critical thinking linked to anti-colonial struggles and announced investments in Brazil's AI Plan for cooperation with Africa, Asia, and Latin America.

item.title: Governo Lula renova contrato de R$ 562 milhões com agências de propaganda
item.description: The Lula government renewed contracts with four advertising agencies for up to R$ 562 million, valid until three months before the 2026 electoral campaign begins. The measure, published by the Secretariat of Social Communication, includes Nova S.A, Calia/Y2 Propaganda and Marketing, Propeg Comunicação, and Agência Nacional de Propaganda. The renewal has sparked debate over the use of public funds in the pre-electoral period.

item.title: Lula deixa TV Brasil em último lugar no Ibope
item.description: TV Brasil recorded the lowest viewership in Greater São Paulo last Friday (22), despite featuring an exclusive interview with President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. The public broadcaster's talk show was the least-watched option among viewers, underscoring its persistent lack of audience appeal. The incident highlights the disconnect between high-profile political content and public engagement with the state-funded network.

item.title: Quem vota em Flávio está entregando a eleição para Lula, diz Zema
item.description: Former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema (Novo) said that voters supporting Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) are effectively handing the election to President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), citing the senator’s declining poll numbers after audio revelations involving banker Daniel Vorcaro. Despite his criticism, Zema stated he would back Flávio in a potential runoff against Lula, emphasizing his goal to oppose the PT. He warned that Flávio’s downward trend is alarming and benefits the left, even as Novo maintains alliances with the PL in several states.

item.title: Motta anuncia transição de um ano para o fim da escala 6×1 e sela acordo com Lula
item.description: House President Hugo Motta announced that the PEC to end the 6×1 work schedule will include a one-year transition to reduce the weekly workweek from 44 to 40 hours in two stages, while maintaining salaries. The agreement, reached after a meeting with President Lula, involves government, Congress, business representatives, and social movements, and includes special provisions for MEI, public servants, and service providers.

item.title: Jornada de 44h por semana cairá para 40h em 1 ano, diz Motta
item.description: House Speaker Hugo Motta announced that the reduction of the workweek from 44 to 40 hours will occur in two phases: 42 hours after 60 days from the PEC’s promulgation, and 40 hours after one year. He stated the transition will balance workers’ demands and productive sector concerns, with no salary reduction, and confirmed the plenary vote is scheduled for May 27.

item.title: Governo Lula envia Janja para evento da ONU em Roma
item.description: The Lula government announced that First Lady Janja Lula da Silva will represent Brazil at the 2026 Nutrition Week in Rome, with all expenses — including travel — covered by the state. The UN-backed event, running until May 28, focuses on hunger, food systems, and coordinated solutions. Janja previously represented Brazil at the 2025 World Food Forum and promotes the Global Alliance Against Hunger in international forums.

item.title: Gestão de Caiado usou fintech suspeita para movimentar R$ 1,3 bi e taxa recaiu sobre comerciantes
item.description: The government of Ronaldo Caiado in Goiás used a fintech suspected of ties to the PCC to move R$1.36 billion in state income transfer programs, according to Coaf documents obtained by Folha. BK Instituição de Pagamento, under investigation by the Federal Police, Federal Revenue, and São Paulo MP, acted as intermediary in disbursements from Goiás' Development Agency. Caiado resigned on March 31 to run for president in 2026.

item.title: Após reunião com Lula, Motta diz que PEC do fim da escala 6x1 prevê jornada de 40 horas sem corte de salário e transição de um ano
item.description: Following a meeting with President Lula, Chamber of Deputies President Hugo Motta stated that the PEC to end the 6x1 work scale will reduce the weekly workweek from 44 to 40 hours without salary cuts, implemented over a one-year transition: a 2-hour reduction after 60 days and another 2 hours after 12 months. He affirmed that ending the 6x1 scale, reducing work hours, and preserving salaries are non-negotiable pillars for Congress and the government.

item.title: Extrema direita tenta 'calar' arte, ciência e professores por 'temer' a educação do povo, diz Lula
item.description: President Lula accused the far right of attempting to silence professors, censor art, and deny science out of fear of popular consciousness through education. He emphasized that universities are bastions of resistance against colonialism, racism, and discrimination, and advocated for Brazil-Africa cooperation for development. Lula also criticized the use of artificial intelligence in electoral campaigns, calling it a 'strategic tool' but warning of 'digital colonialism' as a real and immediate threat.

item.title: A diferença de desempenho entre Joaquim Barbosa e Aldo Rebelo em nova pesquisa presidencial
item.description: The latest Nexus/BTG Pactual poll shows Joaquim Barbosa at 2% in first-round voting intentions for the 2026 Brazilian presidential election, technically tied with several low-performing candidates. This contrasts with the Christian Democracy Party's support for his candidacy and mirrors the weak performance of Aldo Rebelo, who polled at 1% in an earlier survey. Lula leads with 40%, followed by Flávio Bolsonaro at 35%.

item.title: Cientista político vê boa notícia para Flávio nas novas pesquisas: ‘Expectativas muito altas’
item.description: Political scientist Fábio Vasconcellos states that although the scandal involving Flávio Bolsonaro and Banco Master caused wear on the senator’s candidacy, the impact in polls was lower than expected in political circles. Differences among pollsters are attributed to methodologies (phone, online, and in-person), but all indicate some level of wear. Vasconcelos emphasizes that voter reaction is slower and more gradual than social media expectations, and that future developments must be monitored to assess the durability of the effect.

item.title: Fim da escala 6x1 vai prever 2 folgas por semana já em 2026; transição para 40 horas será em 1 ano, diz Motta
item.description: Speaker of the Chamber Hugo Motta announced that the reduction of the workweek from 44 to 40 hours, as proposed in the 6x1 scale PEC, will occur in two stages: an immediate 2-hour reduction within 60 days of promulgation (effective in 2026) and a further 2-hour reduction after 12 months. Two weekly days off, not necessarily consecutive, will be guaranteed from promulgation, with sector-specific regulation via collective bargaining and follow-up bills for MEIs and individual sectors.

item.title: Ao vivo: Após reunião com Lula, Motta fala sobre PEC do fim da 6 X 1
item.description: Chamber of Deputies President Hugo Motta met with President Lula to align details of the PEC proposing the end of the 6x1 work schedule and adoption of the 5x2 model. The meeting preceded the official presentation of the bill, with the government advocating for swift implementation and minimal transitional measures to reduce business impact. Despite pressure from sectors for a longer transition, Planalto allies expect the PEC to advance in 2026.

item.title: Crusoé: Como as dívidas influenciam o voto
item.description: The BTG-Nexus poll shows that 25% of Brazilians have financial debts overdue by more than 30 days. Among this group, 39% intend to vote for Flávio Bolsonaro and 36% for President Lula in the first round, giving the senator a 3-point lead among indebted voters.

item.title: O sinal de alerta para Flávio na nova pesquisa sobre a corrida presidencial
item.description: The new BTG Nexus poll shows that the scandal involving Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and former banker Daniel Vorcaro is hurting his candidacy, with Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva leading at 40% voting intention, followed by Flávio at 35%. Columnist Robson Bonin states that Flávio’s political damage stems not only from the revealed conversations but from his pattern of denial and public distancing from Vorcaro, which voters perceived as dishonest.

item.title: Cidadania articula pré-candidatura de Aécio Neves à Presidência em federação com PSDB
item.description: Cidadania unanimously approved the pre-candidacy of Aécio Neves (PSDB-MG) for President of Brazil under the PSDB/Cidadania federation, with formal PSDB support expected in a meeting on May 26. The candidacy is positioned as an alternative to 'lulobolsonarismo,' emphasizing Neves’ administrative experience and commitment to fiscal responsibility, following his narrow second-round loss in the 2014 presidential election.

item.title: 'Era óbvio que Dark Horse ia dar m*', diz cineasta de Olavo de Carvalho
item.description: Filmmaker Josias Teófilo, associated with Olavo de Carvalho, had previously stated that the biopic about Jair Bolsonaro had the potential to cause damage, even before the audio leak of Flávio Bolsonaro requesting R$134 million from banker Daniel Vorcaro. The comment was made amid growing scrutiny over the film's financing and political implications.

item.title: Convocação de Neymar mostra que Brasil está desesperado para ter 'seu próprio Messi', diz jornal inglês
item.description: The Guardian’s Jonathan Wilson framed Neymar’s 2026 World Cup call-up as a desperate attempt by Brazil to find its own Messi, echoing the redemption narrative of Argentina’s 2022 triumph. The article argues that years of casting Neymar as Messi’s Brazilian counterpart created a toxic dependency culture that hindered team development. Despite his status as Brazil’s all-time top scorer, his return after injury and inconsistency is portrayed as a political act of faith by Ancelotti, lacking clear sporting justification.

item.title: ‘Comédia de erros’: a visão do ‘Financial Times’ sobre o filme ‘Dark Horse’
item.description: The Financial Times labeled the biopic 'Dark Horse' about Jair Bolsonaro a 'comedy of errors' after revelations that Flávio Bolsonaro secured millions in funding from Daniel Vorcaro, a banker suspected of fraud in the collapse of Banco Master. The leaked WhatsApp audio, published by The Intercept Brasil, damaged Flávio's campaign and boosted Lula's lead in the polls, with Datafolha showing Lula at 47% and Flávio at 43% in a hypothetical second-round matchup.

item.title: Lula recibe radioterapia preventiva contra el cáncer de piel a cuatro meses de las elecciones en Brasil
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, 80, has begun preventive radiotherapy consisting of 15 sessions for a previously removed skin cancer lesion on his scalp, four months ahead of Brazil's 2026 elections. His team says the treatment will not disrupt his schedule, but the news has intensified public focus on his health during his reelection campaign.

item.title: Governo teme que Centrão aproveite emenda sobrevivente para resgatar polêmicas
item.description: The Lula government fears that the Centrão bloc will exploit the surviving amendment by Tião Medeiros to the PEC on reducing the workweek to reintroduce controversial elements from Sergio Turra’s withdrawn amendment, which proposed up to 52-hour weekly workdays and a ten-year transition. Concern is growing that, during final negotiations in the special committee and House plenary, the center bloc may seek to embed Turra’s disputed provisions despite public backlash. Lula’s allies are monitoring closely to prevent negative surprises in the final text.

item.title: Filme de Bolsonaro virou ‘comédia de erros’ que ameaça candidatura de Flávio, diz Financial Times
item.description: The Financial Times warns that the film 'Dark Horse', inspired by Jair Bolsonaro’s political trajectory and partially funded by jailed banker Daniel Vorcaro, threatens the 2026 presidential pre-candidacy of his son, Flávio Bolsonaro. The controversy stems from revelations that Flávio sought R$61 million from Vorcaro for the film, placing him at the center of a growing political scandal that could undermine his electoral prospects.

item.title: Lula fará radioterapia para tratar câncer de pele; entenda o carcinoma basocelular
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has begun superficial radiotherapy on his scalp to prevent recurrence of basal cell carcinoma, the most common type of skin cancer in Brazil, following surgery in April. The treatment is preventive and expected to have minimal side effects, as the lesion was localized and detected early. Experts note that while basal cell carcinoma rarely metastasizes, it can cause tissue damage and disfigurement if left untreated, but carries a favorable prognosis when managed promptly.

item.title: O que Ronaldo Caiado pensa sobre chapa com Michelle Bolsonaro
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado stated he was not consulted about the possibility of Michelle Bolsonaro running as his vice-presidential candidate, reiterating that Senator Flávio Bolsonaro remains the party's pre-candidate. He said the vice-presidential decision will be made closer to the August party conventions, but added that his inner circle believes an alliance with Michelle Bolsonaro would be immediately accepted and could lead to a first-round victory over Lula. Caiado also said Flávio Bolsonaro’s justifications regarding his audios with Daniel Vorcaro were not convincing, leaving judgment to the voters.

item.title: BTG/Nexus: Lula amplia vantagem no 2º turno contra Flávio Bolsonaro e venceria por 47% a 43%
item.description: BTG/Nexus poll shows Lula leading with 47% of voting intentions against 43% for Flávio Bolsonaro in a hypothetical 2026 runoff, widening his advantage. Released on May 25, 2026, the survey indicates growing support for the president over the Rio de Janeiro senator.

item.title: Moraes rejeita — mais uma vez — encerrar inquérito contra Geddel por lavagem de dinheiro
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes once again rejected a request to dismiss the money laundering investigation against former minister Geddel Vieira Lima and his brother Lúcio Vieira Lima, which involves alleged simulated contracts for agricultural machinery leasing and cattle trading. Although the defense argued the case stems from Operation Cui Bono—already declared null and final by TRF-1—Moraes ruled the investigation is proceeding normally, with police diligences completed and a PF report filed, making dismissal premature. He stressed that those under investigation cannot dictate the course of the probe, which remains under the Federal Public Prosecutor’s Office for potential indictment.

item.title: Crusoé: A reação da rede social ao marmitex de Zema
item.description: Romeu Zema, former governor of Minas Gerais and pre-candidate for presidency from the Novo party, posted a video showing his weekend meal prep, emphasizing he lives alone and doesn’t know how to cook. The clip sparked reactions on social media, becoming a subject of memes and commentary about his attempt to project a simple, relatable image. The article was first published by O Antagonista and later shared by Crusoé.

item.title: Às vésperas das eleições, Lula renova R$ 562 mi em contratos de propaganda
item.description: The Lula government renewed institutional advertising contracts worth R$ 562.5 million just months before the 2026 elections. The contract amendments were published on March 25, involving the four main firms already providing communication services to the federal government. The move raises concerns about the use of public funds during the pre-election period.

item.title: Governo Lula publica anúncio de uma página no “Globo” pelo fim da 6 X 1
item.description: The Lula government published a full-page ad in O Globo newspaper advocating for the end of the 6x1 work schedule, emphasizing that reducing the workweek to 40 hours without pay cuts will benefit 35 million formally employed workers. The ad frames free time as a right and notes the policy has already been applied to 60,000 outsourced public workers. This move is part of Lula’s re-election strategy, involving political negotiations in Congress, including a meeting with House President Hugo Motta and awaiting the final report from rapporteur Leo Prates.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro vai aos EUA e aguarda reunião com Trump
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) arrived in the United States on May 25, 2026, awaiting a meeting with Donald Trump scheduled for May 26, following an alleged White House invitation. His team expressed concern over possible cancellation due to Trump’s ongoing Iran negotiations, which kept him in Washington. Bolsonaro aims to use the meeting to highlight revelations about audio recordings with banker Daniel Vorcaro and is expected to meet with senior State Department officials.

item.title: Rachadinha, relação com Vorcaro e emendas na mira de Dino: a situação de Mário Frias em meio a desgaste com 'Dark Horse'
item.description: Federal deputy Mário Frias (PL-SP) is under investigation by the PGR for alleged 'rachadinha', after a former employee stated she returned part of her salary to his chief of staff with his knowledge between 2023 and 2024, and used consigned loans to pay off 2022 campaign debts. Minister Flávio Dino (STF) also demanded information on amendments sent by Frias to an NGO linked to the film 'Dark Horse', of which Frias is executive producer, amid money laundering suspicions. PT and PSOL filed complaints with the PGR and requested investigation by the House Ethics Council.

item.title: Filme de Bolsonaro ameaça campanha de Flávio, diz Financial Times
item.description: The Financial Times warned that the Bolsonaro biopic 'Dark Horse', funded by investigated businessman Daniel Vorcaro, threatens to undermine Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential pre-campaign as he seeks to fill his father's political space. The film, initially denied as having received Vorcaro's funds, was exposed by Intercept Brasil, revealing a $24 million deal and an audio where Flávio demands overdue payments, drawing criticism from allies for treating the public as 'idiots'.

item.title: PEC da 6×1 entra em semana decisiva após reunião de Lula e Motta
item.description: The 6×1 workweek PEC, which reduces the weekly workload from 44 to 40 hours without salary reduction, enters a decisive phase in the Chamber of Deputies following a meeting between Lula, Hugo Motta, and Luiz Marinho. Relator Léo Prates is expected to release the report between Monday and Tuesday, with a vote planned in the special committee. The main point of contention remains the transition timeline, with the government pushing for immediate implementation and congressional and business sectors advocating for a gradual shift to minimize economic impacts.

item.title: Corpus Christi é feriado ou ponto facultativo? Veja o que muda no funcionamento pelo país
item.description: Corpus Christi, celebrated on June 4, 2026, is a movable Catholic religious holiday commemorating the institution of the Eucharist. While observed as a holiday in some Brazilian cities and states, the federal government treats it as an optional point, allowing public employees to choose whether to work. The day is marked by processions, masses, and the tradition of colorful sawdust and salt carpets in the streets, a custom inherited from Portuguese influence.

item.title: Nexus reforça Datafolha e AtlasIntel e indica queda de Flávio
item.description: The BTG/Nexus electoral poll released on Monday, 25, shows Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) losing to Lula (PT) in a potential runoff, reinforcing the downward trend previously indicated by AtlasIntel and Datafolha. Lula leads with 47% of voting intentions, amid fallout from leaked messages involving Bolsonaro’s son and banker Daniel Vorcaro.

item.title: Governo Lula é avaliado como ruim ou péssimo por 40%; bom e ótimo somam 37%, diz pesquisa BTG/Nexus
item.description: The BTG/Nexus poll shows improved evaluation of Lula's government, with 40% rating it as bad or terrible (down 3 points) and 37% as good or excellent (up 4 points). Approval stands at 47% and disapproval at 48%, indicating a technical tie. Economic perception improved (39% positive vs 33% in April), and 73% support ending the 'small package tax', although 25% of families still have overdue debts.

item.title: JOTA Principal: Negociações da PEC do fim da escala 6×1 devem mobilizar governo e Câmara nesta semana
item.description: The Lula government is pushing to vote on a PEC reducing the workweek from 44 to 40 hours, with a meeting between President Lula and House Speaker Hugo Motta to finalize the text. Rapporteur Leo Prates will present the report in the special committee on Tuesday (25), with expectations of a plenary vote this week, despite high quorum requirements and unresolved transition details. Meanwhile, Flávio Bolsonaro traveled to the U.S. to seek a meeting with Donald Trump, aiming to shift focus from his political troubles tied to Daniel Vorcaro, whose return to a special PF cell was approved by Minister André Mendonça.

item.title: Nunes Marques terá reunião com presidentes dos TREs
item.description: TSE President Nunes Marques will meet with all TRE presidents on Monday to hear state-level demands, focusing on organized crime and electronic voting machine maintenance. He also plans meetings with political party leaders to prepare for the 2026 elections.

item.title: 48% desaprovam o governo Lula e 47% aprovam, diz Nexus
item.description: The Nexus poll released on May 25, 2026 shows a technical tie in approval of President Lula’s government, with 48% disapproving and 47% approving, within the 2-point margin of error. The survey of 2,045 voters conducted May 22–24, 2026, is registered with the TSE as BR-04193/2026 and funded by BTG Pactual.
